standard_prerequisites.name: Homotopy of morphisms
standard_prerequisites.statement: A morphism is homotopic to zero when it is the differential of a degree-minus-one map.

core_obligations: Set up the sequence and the diagram: apply axiom (C) to the identity morphism to get the admissible short exact sequence, and display its structure maps with their degrees (source lines 3875-3885).

Write the identity of the cone in terms of the splitting: use the defining identities of the cone to express the identity as the sum of a pi and s b, and then use the differential identities to rewrite that sum (source lines 3886-3890).

Exhibit the homotopy: observe that the resulting expression is the differential of the composite s pi, using that s has degree minus one, so the identity is homotopic to zero (source lines 3890-3892).

proof_roadmap.step: Apply axiom (C) to the identity morphism and display the structure maps.
Rewrite the identity of the cone as a pi + s b and simplify it.
Recognise the result as d(s pi) and conclude the homotopy.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-id-cone-null at source lines 3866-3872: in the standing situation (a dg category with the distinguished-triangle axioms) the identity morphism on the cone of an identity morphism is homotopic to zero. The proof at source lines 3874-3893 is a short computation that has to be set up carefully. It uses the admissible short exact sequence supplied by axiom (C) for the identity morphism, writes down the diagram with the structure maps a, b, pi, s and their degrees, and then computes the identity of the cone as a composition of those maps, rewrites it using the identities from the splitting of the sequence, and recognises the result as the differential of the composite s pi, which exhibits the required homotopy. The sign and degree bookkeeping (s has degree minus one, and the differential of the composite is what makes the last equality hold) is the substance, and the statement records only the conclusion. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
